scope.description: Single-voter in-process cluster at protocol version 3 with 50ms timeouts whose log store is a CommitTrackingLogStore. The node runs and commits five commands with RestoreCommittedLogs disabled, so nothing is staged; it is then restarted with the flag enabled and the staged value still zero, commits two further commands so the flag-on path stages a commit index, and is restarted once more with the flag still enabled. Every phase records the staged commit index, the configuration size and whether a leader appears.
assumptions: tryStageCommitIndex returns early when RestoreCommittedLogs is disabled, so a cluster that has only ever run with the flag off has no staged commit index even though its log holds committed entries; the observation records the staged value rather than assuming it.
The two restarts differ only in whether the store has a staged commit index at that moment, so any difference in the outcome is attributable to that value rather than to the flag alone.
excluded: No multi-voter cluster and no configuration change: the question is which condition triggers the loss, not what the loss causes.

basis.prefix: Real bootstrap, real election, real commits with the flag disabled, graceful shutdown, restart with the flag enabled, real commits while enabled, graceful shutdown, restart again with the flag enabled, all on the same InmemCommitTrackingStore/InmemStore/InmemSnapshotStore instances. Nothing is fabricated.

comparisons.description: The first restart with the flag enabled, before anything has been staged, must keep the configuration.

The next restart with the flag enabled, after the flag-on path has staged a commit index, must still keep the configuration; this is the comparison that decides whether the trigger is the flag or the staged commit index.
